## 1. A full-six-coordinate candidate, not an assigned phase update

Use zero-based indices x=(a0,a1,a2,a3,a4,a5), relative to a chosen actual reference Cell. Define

T(x)=(-a5,a0,a1,a2,a3,a4).

Each positive axis maps to the next positive axis, except e5 -> -e0. Thus T sends every primitive signed-axis displacement to another, is bijective, and preserves sum(a_j^2). Direct composition gives T^6=-I and T^12=I. Its order is exactly 12, as witnessed by the orbit of e0. Also (T^3)^2=-I on the full raw coordinate module; this is an algebraic relation, not a redefinition of native angles.

T is not a single primitive displacement. Treating x -> T(x) as a physical point path requires a declared sequence of axis steps and its timing. Counting T applications as heartbeats is not authorized. Even T^12 returning raw coordinates does not erase the retained operation history or return physical time.

The polynomial label f_x(t)=sum(a_j*t^j) in Z[t]/(t^6+1) is an exact coefficient encoding. Multiplication by t induces precisely T. Ring multiplication is representation algebra, not an asserted native material multiplication law.

## 2. Why one Euler readout loses two integer coordinates

Factor t^6+1=(t^2+1)(t^4-t^2+1). Choose alpha in the first-quadrant embedding of Phi_12(alpha)=0, so alpha^6=-1. Define rho12(x)=f_x(alpha). Then the raw-coordinate rule, not an independently edited phase tag, proves

rho12(Tx)=alpha*rho12(x).

The reduced coefficient tuple c=(c0,c1,c2,c3) is

c=(a0-a4, a1-a5, a2+a4, a3+a5).

Its update is exactly c -> (-c3,c0,c1+c3,c2), reproducing the preceding four-coefficient recurrence as an observer of T.

Since Phi_12 has degree four and is irreducible over Q, the integer kernel is exactly

ker(rho12)={(s,t,-s,-t,s,t):s,t in Z}.

Proof: c=0 forces a0=a4=s, a1=a5=t, a2=-s, a3=-t, and conversely substitution gives zero. These are two independent INTEGER degrees of freedom, not two new spatial dimensions and not necessarily small errors. Kernel states remain invisible to rho12 under every power of T, by the intertwining identity.

## 3. Exact repair, with integral gluing rather than a free product

Introduce beta^2=-1 and rho4(x)=f_x(beta)=h0+h1*beta, where

h0=a0-a2+a4; h1=a1-a3+a5.

Then h -> (-h1,h0) under T. In the two distinct observer evaluations beta may be embedded as alpha^3; evaluating f at beta is not the same as evaluating f at alpha. On the rho12 kernel, h=(3s,3t).

The joint map x -> (c,h) has exactly this image:

h0-c0+c2 == 0 (mod 3),
h1-c1+c3 == 0 (mod 3).

Indeed these two expressions equal 3a4 and 3a5. Conversely, for compatible integer data let

s=(h0-c0+c2)/3; t=(h1-c1+c3)/3.

Then the UNIQUE raw state is

x=(c0+s,c1+t,c2-s,c3-t,s,t).

This proves injectivity and sufficiency, and shows the image has index 9 in Z^4 x Z^2. The divisions recover integers already required by the image condition; they do not divide a native Cell. Four visible coefficients plus two repair coefficients have total additive rank six; this is a statement about this linear representation, not a lower bound against arbitrary nonlinear encodings.

## 4. A coordinate-level residual-revelation operation

Declare U(x)=(a0,a1,a2,a3,-a4,-a5). It is another signed-axis/adjacency/length-preserving candidate and U^2=I. It reverses two coordinate axes, rather than editing phases at fixed raw states. Given compatible (c,h) and s,t from section 3,

c'=(c0+2s,c1+2t,c2-2s,c3-2t),
h'=(h0-2s,h1-2t).

The representation is therefore closed and exact for every finite word in {T,U}: verify each generator and induct on word length. Source IDs, positive branch data, relation labels and operation history remain separate and retained.

An explicit equal-length, equal-mass and equal-readout witness is

xA=(1,0,0,0,2,0), xB=(-1,0,2,0,0,0).

Each is placed on one branch of weight 1 with the SAME source ID and empty history in its respective alternative experiment. Both have CWM=(1,1,1), native length square 5, c=(-1,0,2,0), and rho12=-1+2alpha^2. Their h are (3,0) and (-3,0).

After the SAME operation U:

UxA=(1,0,0,0,-2,0), cA'=(3,0,-2,0), hA'=(-1,0);
UxB=(-1,0,2,0,0,0), cB'=(-1,0,2,0), hB'=(-3,0).

The exact squared-modulus observer is 3 for both before U and 7 versus 3 afterwards. All four positive CWM states stay (1,1,1); all raw squared lengths stay 5. This is an algebraic observer contrast, NOT extra mass, measured detector intensity, energy creation, decoherence or quantum entanglement.

## 5. A conservation identity for visible and hidden integer data

For c=(c0,c1,c2,c3), define

A(c)=c0^2+c1^2+c2^2+c3^2+c0*c2+c1*c3,
B(c)=c0*c1+c1*c2+c2*c3.

Algebraic conjugation in the first-quadrant embedding yields |rho12|^2=A+B*sqrt(3). The implementation retains the exact pair (A,B); it never evaluates sqrt(3) numerically. Expanding the integer coordinate definitions proves the stronger purely rational identity

3*sum(a_j^2)=2*A(c)+h0^2+h1^2.

For the witness xA, the right side changes from 2*3+9 to 2*7+1, both 15. For xB it remains 2*3+9. Thus a single visible scalar can change while the combined invariant is preserved. A is a coefficient quadratic form, not generally the physical squared amplitude; B need not vanish outside this witness. No physical energy interpretation is attached to either term.

The pair (rho12(x),rho12(Ux)) uniquely determines x. In coefficients c and u, recover

s=(u0-c0)/2, t=(u1-c1)/2,

and then x by section 3's reconstruction. Admissible measurements have even differences and u2=c2-2s, u3=c3-2t. Therefore one controlled extra coordinate operation plus a second exact algebraic readout resolves the entire two-integer kernel. The first readout alone does not. This is an exact model observer result, not an assumption of a nondisturbing physical measurement.
